entry_state: Inventory sales and recoveries retain only unsold cost and allowance. A net hedge preserves gross transactions and their earnings periods, including nil-position eligibility. Award accounting then separates service and market conditions, cancellation, remeasured cash liabilities and settlement choice. Beneficial amendments preserve original cost and add their own service clock; cash-to-equity conversion removes the measured liability and recognizes the signed difference without supplying a valuation model.
exit_state: Ordinary EPS requires allocating earnings under the actual participation rights before division and recalculating that allocation after assumed issuance. The capped-family ordering proof requires complete additive gross effects; a shared threshold bonus breaks those effects and leaves general selection unresolved despite correct conditional worlds. Contingent options additionally require an admitted similar option's assumed exercise. The participating-dividend tax example retains a signed residual across years, so its negative year-three adjustment reverses earlier allocation without becoming a cash dividend or a tax-loss asset.

findings.judgment: The two-class example allocates declared dividends and undistributed earnings to the rights-bearing classes, giving ordinary EPS 1 rather than the erroneous 1.2. Future service value enters option proceeds separately from award expense. The cash/share choice example also reverses the liability expense under assumed equity treatment; adding shares while freezing earnings at 90 would compute the wrong hypothetical world.

A senior cumulative entitlement and residual cap are introduced by concrete profit cases before the min/max formula. Negative ordinary allocations follow from the stated absence of preference loss-sharing. Adding 50 assumed shares changes both participation and denominator, yielding 12/17 rather than 2/3. The ordering argument uses the same additive gross effect in both cap regimes and explicitly separates its local derivation from IAS 33's dilution requirements. The method's 49 finite combinations do not establish a general dependent-selection rule.

The common threshold bonus makes the first conversion's after-tax increment 12 and the second's increment 8; summing isolated increments overstates earnings by 4. The joint equations define the supplied bonus and tax model before interpretation. At initial profit 80 each isolated conversion raises EPS while the combined world lowers it; the manuscript correctly declines to substitute global minimization for the individual-series requirements. Inspected official examples with fixed increments are not represented as settling this dependence.

The contingent option example distinguishes a satisfied period-end store condition from a forecast and separately requires assumed exercise of an admitted similar outstanding option. With strikes 6 and 5, incremental shares are 8 and 10, yielding 50/59. Raising the prerequisite strike to 12 excludes both despite the contingent option's isolated dilution. The explicit similarity finding, open contingency period and no-future-service premises remain visible.

The June 2017 interpretation motivates adding the ordinary holders' share of a hypothetical participating-dividend tax benefit before any payment. Current profit, declared dividends and their actual tax benefit are kept separate. The three-year table carries residual -550 and adjustment -150 in year three, giving ordinary earnings 40; clipping the adjustment at zero would double-count earlier benefit. The derived payout cancellation is restricted to fixed rights, supplied deductibility and recognition facts, and the source's specified payout pattern.

source_limit: Author rendered reading of conditional EPS methods and cited interpretive support. No new standards-source inspection, accounting admission or calculator execution occurred. General nonadditive dilution selection, actual rights/tax applicability and independent technical/domain/human acceptance remain open.
